title: Thousands cheering in New Jersey on 9/11?
claim: Thousands and thousands of people were cheering
summary: Independent investigations found no evidence for the thousands-strong celebrations in New Jersey described by Trump.

title: The claim that Mexico sends criminals to the U.S.
claim: The Mexican government ... they send the bad ones over
summary: PolitiFact found no evidence that the Mexican government was deliberately sending criminals across the border. Date denotes the 2015 campaign period, not a verified exact quotation date.

title: The 2020 election was stolen
claim: Claims of a stolen 2020 presidential election
summary: Joe Biden won the 2020 election. Recounts, court proceedings and election officials did not establish fraud sufficient to overturn the result. This is a recurring claim; the date is the election-call milestone, not a specific quotation.

title: COVID-19 risk downplayed
claim: Repeated statements minimizing the public-health threat from COVID-19
summary: PolitiFact documented repeated downplaying of COVID-19's threat in its review of Trump's record. This is a topic overview, not a rating of one exact quote.

title: COVID-19 was used to cheat in the 2020 election
claim: Democrats used the COVID-19 pandemic to cheat in the 2020 presidential election
summary: PolitiFact rated this allegation Pants on Fire and found no evidence for the sweeping fraud claim.

title: Who actually pays tariffs?
claim: Tariffs are paid by foreign countries rather than U.S. importers and consumers
summary: Tariffs are collected from U.S. importers, and their costs can be distributed among importers, businesses, foreign producers and consumers. The foreign-country-pays framing is inaccurate.

title: Did Trump inherit record inflation?
claim: Inflation was at record levels when Trump returned to office
summary: FactCheck.org found the description of inherited inflation as being at record levels false.

sources.label: FactCheck.org State of the Union review

title: Did a cognitive test prove 'extreme intelligence'?
claim: Cognitive test results showed extreme intelligence
summary: A cognitive screening test does not measure IQ or establish extreme intelligence. PolitiFact rated the claim False.

title: Did the U.S. attract $20 trillion in foreign investment?
claim: An unprecedented $20 trillion has been invested in the U.S. from outside countries and companies
summary: FactCheck.org described the $20 trillion claim as unsupported, with no substantiated total matching the assertion.

title: October 2026 rally claims under scrutiny
claim: Repeated claims on inflation, crime and immigration during October midterm rallies
summary: FactCheck.org reviewed more than a dozen false, misleading or exaggerated statements made during multiple October rallies. This entry links to their analysis; it is not a verdict on one quotation.
